records.source: Φοβηθῶμεν οὖν μήποτε καταλειπομένης ἐπαγγελίας εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσιν αὐτοῦ δοκῇ τις ἐξ ὑμῶν ὑστερηκέναι·
records.gloss: Let us fear therefore lest, being left a promise to enter into the rest of him, seem anyone of you to have fallen short;
pieces: So, while the promise that we may enter {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rest is still open, let us be afraid that any one of you might be found to have missed it.

L.1: Therefore let us fear lest, while a promise of entering into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rest is left [open], any of you should seem to have fallen short;

R.1: God's promise that we may enter {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rest is still open. So we should be afraid that any of you might fail to reach it.

decisions.choice: let us fear: a serious, healthy fear of missing what God offers
decisions.reason: The author means real fear, the kind that takes God's warning seriously (10:31; 12:28-29), not panic. The wilderness generation is the warning.

decisions.choice: while a promise is left: the promise was not used up when that generation failed
decisions.reason: καταλειπομένης means "being left behind", still remaining. The argument of 4:6-9 explains why the promise still stands.

decisions.choice: seem: be judged, be shown to have fallen short
alternatives: think (that he has come too late)
decisions.reason: δοκέω may mean "be found" or "seem": even the appearance of falling short is to be feared. It can also mean "think", so that the warning is against anyone thinking he has come too late for the promise. The first fits the stern tone of the passage better.

decisions.choice: fallen short: failed to reach, come too late
decisions.reason: The picture is of arriving too late, or falling behind on a journey and not reaching the goal.

decisions.choice: [open]
decisions.reason: Literal adds what "left" means here.

decisions.choice: missed it; fail to reach it
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what falling short of the promise means.

records.heading: The rest that remains for God's people

records.source: καὶ γάρ ἐσμεν εὐηγγελισμένοι καθάπερ κἀκεῖνοι, ἀλλ’ οὐκ ὠφέλησεν ὁ λόγος τῆς ἀκοῆς ἐκείνους, μὴ συγκεκερασμένους τῇ πίστει τοῖς ἀκούσασιν.
records.gloss: And for we are having had good news announced just as also those; but not benefited the word of the hearing those, not having been joined together by the faith with the [ones] having heard.
pieces: For we too have been told good news, as they were. But the message they heard did them no good, because they did not join in faith with those who truly listened.

L.2: For indeed we have had good news announced [to us], just as those also; but the word of hearing did not benefit those, since they were not joined together by faith with those who heard.

R.2: We have heard good news, just as they did. But the message did not help them. They did not join in faith with the people who really listened to it.

decisions.choice: had good news announced: God's promise of rest was good news for them and is good news for us
decisions.reason: The verb belongs with the noun for the gospel. For the wilderness generation the good news was God's promise of the land and of rest; for the readers it is the message of salvation spoken by the Lord (2:3).

decisions.choice: the word of hearing: the message they heard
decisions.reason: A Hebrew-shaped phrase for a message that is heard (compare 1 Thessalonians 2:13).

decisions.choice: they were not joined in faith with those who heard
alternatives: the word did not benefit them, because it was not mixed with faith in those who heard it
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT has the plural form συγκεκερασμένους, agreeing with "those": the people of the wilderness were not joined in faith with those who truly heard, that is, who listened and obeyed, such as Joshua and Caleb (Numbers 14:6-9). From general knowledge, this reading is found in P13, P46, Codex Alexandrinus, Codex Vaticanus and most manuscripts. A few manuscripts, Codex Sinaiticus among them, have the singular, agreeing with "the word": the word was not mixed with faith in those who heard it, which is the reading of the King James Version. Other manuscripts reword the last phrase. The singular is easier to understand, which may be why it arose. Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: heard: heard and responded
decisions.reason: Hearing in the full biblical sense is listening and obeying (3:7, "if you hear his voice").

decisions.choice: those who truly listened; the people who really listened to it
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the full sense of hearing, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: good news
decisions.reason: The verb is rendered "have good news announced" or "be told good news", since the good news here includes the promise given to Israel.

records.source: εἰσερχόμεθα γὰρ εἰς κατάπαυσιν οἱ πιστεύσαντες, καθὼς εἴρηκεν· Ὡς ὤμοσα ἐν τῇ ὀργῇ μου, Εἰ εἰσελεύσονται εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσίν μου, καίτοι τῶν ἔργων ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου γενηθέντων, εἴρηκεν γάρ που περὶ τῆς ἑβδόμης οὕτως· Καὶ κατέπαυσεν ὁ θεὸς ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ἑβδόμῃ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐν τούτῳ πάλιν· Εἰ εἰσελεύσονται εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσίν μου.
records.gloss: We enter for into rest the [ones] having believed, just as he has said: As I swore in the anger of me, If they will enter into the rest of me, although the works from foundation of world having come about, \v 4 he has said for somewhere about the seventh thus: And rested the God on the day the seventh from all the works of him, \v 5 and in this again: If they will enter into the rest of me.
pieces: For it is we who have believed who enter that rest, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has said, "So in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger I swore an oath: 'They will never enter {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rest.'" Yet {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} works had been finished since the world was founded.
For somewhere {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has spoken of the seventh day in these words: "And God rested on the seventh day from all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} works."
And in this passage again: "They will never enter {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rest."

L.3: For we who have believed enter into rest, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has said, "As I swore in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger, 'They will not enter into {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rest,'" although the works were finished from [the] foundation of [the] world.
L.4: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has said somewhere about the seventh [day] thus: "And God rested on the seventh day from all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} works";
L.5: and in this [place] again: "They will not enter into {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rest."

R.3: We who have believed are the ones who enter that rest. God said, "So in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger I swore an oath: 'They will never enter {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rest.'" His work had been finished long before, ever since the world began.
R.4: In another place God speaks about the seventh day like this: "On the seventh day God rested from all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work."
R.5: And in the psalm {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says again, "They will never enter {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rest."

decisions.choice: we enter: believers enter God's rest now, and are still to enter it fully
decisions.reason: The present tense says that believers are already entering; yet 4:11 still urges them to make every effort to enter. The rest is begun by faith and completed at the end.

decisions.choice: Psalm 95:11 (94:11 Greek)
decisions.reason: The oath of the psalm quoted in 3:11 is quoted again, whole in 4:3 and in part in 4:5.

decisions.choice: God's works were finished at creation, so his rest has stood open since then
decisions.reason: The point is that the rest of the psalm is not only the land: it is God's own rest, which has existed since he finished his works. The wilderness generation failed to enter a rest that was already there.

decisions.choice: somewhere: a way of citing Scripture without naming the place
decisions.reason: The author does not mean he is unsure where the words are (compare 2:6); what matters is that God said them.

decisions.choice: Genesis 2:2
decisions.reason: The words follow the Greek of Genesis 2:2.

decisions.choice: he has said: God is the speaker of Scripture
decisions.reason: Throughout the letter Scripture is quoted as God speaking (1:5-13; 4:7), so the subject is God.

decisions.choice: rest
decisions.reason: "Rest" at every level, as in 3:11. Literal keeps "into rest" without the article; Balanced and Readable say "that rest".

decisions.choice: his works (God's works); the seventh day
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name whose works they were and supply "day".

decisions.choice: in the psalm
decisions.reason: Readable says which passage: Psalm 95, quoted in 3:7-11.

records.source: ἐπεὶ οὖν ἀπολείπεται τινὰς εἰσελθεῖν εἰς αὐτήν, καὶ οἱ πρότερον εὐαγγελισθέντες οὐκ εἰσῆλθον δι’ ἀπείθειαν, πάλιν τινὰ ὁρίζει ἡμέραν, Σήμερον, ἐν Δαυὶδ λέγων μετὰ τοσοῦτον χρόνον, καθὼς προείρηται, Σήμερον ἐὰν τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ ἀκούσητε, μὴ σκληρύνητε τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν·
records.gloss: Since therefore it remains some to enter into it, and the [ones] formerly having had good news announced not entered because of disobedience, \v 7 again a certain he sets day, Today, in David saying after so long time, just as it has been said before: Today if the voice of him you hear, not harden the hearts of you;
pieces: So it is still left for some to enter that rest, and those who first heard the good news did not go in, because they would not obey.

For this reason God again marks out a certain day, "Today," speaking through David so long afterward, as was said above: "Today, if you hear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice, do not harden your hearts."

L.6: Since therefore it remains for some to enter into it, and those who formerly had good news announced [to them] did not enter because of disobedience,
L.7: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} again sets a certain day, "Today," saying in David after so long a time, just as it has been said before: "Today, if you hear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice, do not harden your hearts."

R.6: So the way into that rest is still open for some to enter. Those who first heard the good news did not go in, because they did not obey.
R.7: So God set another day, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} calls it "Today." Long afterward {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke of it through David, in the words we read above: "Today, if you hear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice, do not make your hearts hard."

decisions.choice: disobedience: refusing to obey
decisions.reason: As in 3:18-19, disobedience and unbelief are one failure seen from two sides.

decisions.choice: in David: through David, or in the book of Psalms that bears his name
decisions.reason: The Hebrew Psalm 95 has no title, but in the Greek psalm it is headed as David's. Either way the psalm was spoken long after Joshua led the people into the land, so God's offer of rest was still open.

decisions.choice: God fixes a day and names it "Today"
decisions.reason: ὁρίζω means to set or appoint a time; God appoints a new day of opportunity.

decisions.choice: Psalm 95:7-8 (94:7-8 Greek)
decisions.reason: Quoted already in 3:7-8 and 3:15; "as has been said before" points back to those places.

decisions.choice: Today
decisions.reason: As in 3:7.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: The subject is God, as in 4:3-4.

decisions.choice: two sentences: "So it is still left ..."; "For this reason God ..."
decisions.reason: Balanced splits the long sentence and says how the two parts are linked.

records.source: εἰ γὰρ αὐτοὺς Ἰησοῦς κατέπαυσεν, οὐκ ἂν περὶ ἄλλης ἐλάλει μετὰ ταῦτα ἡμέρας.
records.gloss: If for them Joshua gave rest, not would about another he speak after these [things] day.
pieces: If Joshua had brought them into rest, God would not afterward speak of a different day.

L.8: For if Joshua had given them rest, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would not speak about another day after these [things].

R.8: Joshua led the people into the land, but that was not the rest God meant. If Joshua had given them that rest, God would not have gone on, years later, to speak about another day.

decisions.choice: Joshua, son of Nun
decisions.reason: In Greek, Joshua's name is the same as the name Jesus; both come from the Hebrew name Yehoshua. Here it means Joshua, who led Israel into the land. The reader of the Greek hears the echo: the first Joshua could not give the final rest, but Jesus leads God's children into glory (2:10; 4:14).

decisions.choice: Joshua 21:44; 22:4; Deuteronomy 12:9-10
decisions.reason: The book of Joshua says that God gave Israel rest in the land. The author argues that this was not the final rest, because Psalm 95, written later, still offers it.

decisions.choice: a condition contrary to fact: Joshua did not give the final rest
decisions.reason: The form of the sentence assumes the first part is not true. The subject of "would speak" is God, the speaker of the psalm.

decisions.choice: Joshua
decisions.reason: Every level says "Joshua", the person meant; an older English Bible rendered the name "Jesus" here.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: The subject is God.

decisions.choice: Joshua led the people into the land, but that was not the rest God meant.
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the step the argument assumes.

records.source: ἄρα ἀπολείπεται σαββατισμὸς τῷ λαῷ τοῦ θεοῦ·
records.gloss: So remains a Sabbath rest for the people of the God;
pieces: So a Sabbath rest is still waiting for God's people.

L.9: So then a Sabbath rest remains for the people of God;

R.9: So God's people still have a Sabbath rest waiting for them.

decisions.choice: Sabbath rest: a festive keeping of Sabbath, sharing God's seventh-day rest
decisions.reason: Here the author changes from κατάπαυσις to σαββατισμός, a word made from "Sabbath". No earlier use of it is known in surviving Greek writing. It ties the rest that remains to God's rest on the seventh day (4:4, 4:10): God's people are to share the joy and completion of his own Sabbath.

decisions.choice: so then: the conclusion of 4:3-8
decisions.reason: Since the psalm speaks of rest long after Joshua, the rest is still to come.

decisions.choice: Sabbath rest
decisions.reason: A different word from "rest" elsewhere in the passage, so it is rendered differently at every level.

records.source: ὁ γὰρ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς κατέπαυσεν ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ ὥσπερ ἀπὸ τῶν ἰδίων ὁ θεός.
records.gloss: The [one] for having entered into the rest of him also himself rested from the works of him just as from the own the God.
pieces: For whoever has entered God's rest has come to rest from {{gender:their|his}} own works too, just as God did from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}.

L.10: For the [one] who has entered into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rest has also rested from {{gender:their|his}} works, just as God [did] from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own.

R.10: When people enter God's rest, they stop their own work, as God stopped {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work on the seventh day.

decisions.choice: his rest: God's rest
decisions.reason: As in 4:1 and 4:3, the rest is God's.

decisions.choice: the one who has entered: any believer who enters God's rest
alternatives: Jesus, who entered God's rest when he finished his work
decisions.reason: The general statements around this verse (4:3, 4:11) suggest that anyone who enters is meant. The singular and the past tense have led some to read it of Jesus, who sat down after making purification for sins (1:3; 10:12) and has gone ahead of us (6:20).

decisions.choice: resting from one's works, as God rested from his
alternatives: ceasing to rely on good deeds
decisions.reason: The picture comes from Genesis 2:2: God finished his works and rested. Those who enter his rest share it. The verse is about entering rest, not about deeds and earning, which is a different subject (Romans 4:4-5).

decisions.choice: God's rest
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name whose rest it is.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The one who enters is anyone, man or woman.

decisions.choice: on the seventh day
decisions.reason: Readable reminds the reader of 4:4.

records.source: σπουδάσωμεν οὖν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς ἐκείνην τὴν κατάπαυσιν, ἵνα μὴ ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ τις ὑποδείγματι πέσῃ τῆς ἀπειθείας.
records.gloss: Let us be eager therefore to enter into that the rest, so that not in the same anyone example falls of the disobedience.
pieces: So let us make it our urgent aim to enter that rest, so that no one falls into the same pattern of disobedience.

L.11: Let us therefore be eager to enter into that rest, so that no one falls in the same example of disobedience.

R.11: So let us work hard to enter that rest. Then none of us will fall by disobeying God, as they did.

decisions.choice: be eager: make haste, put real effort into it
decisions.reason: σπουδάζω means hurrying, being in earnest. It is urgency in holding to faith (4:3), not earning the rest.

decisions.choice: example: a pattern to be avoided
decisions.reason: ὑπόδειγμα is a model or example. The wilderness generation is a warning pattern of disobedience. Later in the letter the same word means a copy of the heavenly sanctuary (8:5; 9:23).

decisions.choice: fall: come to ruin, as their bodies fell in the wilderness
decisions.reason: The verb picks up 3:17.

decisions.choice: by disobeying God, as they did
alternatives: in the same example of disobedience
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly whose example it is.

records.source: Ζῶν γὰρ ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐνεργὴς καὶ τομώτερος ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν μάχαιραν δίστομον καὶ διϊκνούμενος ἄχρι μερισμοῦ ψυχῆς καὶ πνεύματος, ἁρμῶν τε καὶ μυελῶν, καὶ κριτικὸς ἐνθυμήσεων καὶ ἐννοιῶν καρδίας·
records.gloss: Living for [is] the word of the God and active and sharper beyond every sword two-mouthed and piercing as far as division of soul and of spirit, of joints both and of marrows, and able to judge of thoughts and of intentions of heart;
pieces: For the word of God is alive and at work, and it has a keener edge than any two-edged sword. It reaches right in, cutting through soul and spirit, through joints and marrow, and it weighs the thoughts and purposes of the heart.

L.12: For living [is] the word of God, and at work, and sharper than any two-mouthed sword, and piercing as far as [the] dividing of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and able to judge [the] thoughts and purposes of [the] heart;

R.12: God's word is alive, and it is at work. It is sharper than any sword, even one with two edges. It goes all the way in, through soul and spirit, through joints and marrow. It judges what we think and what we intend in our hearts.

decisions.choice: the word of God: what God says, here the word of Psalm 95 that still speaks "Today"
decisions.reason: The passage has been about God speaking in the psalm (3:7; 4:2, 4:7). That word is alive: it calls and warns now, and it judges. It is not here a title of Christ.

decisions.choice: at work: active, effective
decisions.reason: ἐνεργής describes something that is working and has effect (Philemon 6; 1 Corinthians 16:9).

decisions.choice: a two-mouthed sword: a sword sharpened on both edges
decisions.reason: The edge of a sword is pictured as a mouth that devours (Proverbs 5:4; Revelation 1:16).

decisions.choice: it reaches the innermost parts of a person
alternatives: it separates the soul from the spirit as two parts
decisions.reason: The pairs "soul and spirit" and "joints and marrow" are a picture of reaching as deep as anything can go. The author is not teaching how soul and spirit differ.

decisions.choice: able to judge the thoughts and purposes of the heart
decisions.reason: κριτικός means able to judge or sift. ἐνθύμησις are thoughts or reflections; ἔννοια are intentions, what a person has in mind.

decisions.choice: two-mouthed
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of the Greek word.

decisions.choice: at work; weighs, judges
decisions.reason: Plain words for what the word of God does.

decisions.choice: four short sentences
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the sentence into its parts.

records.source: καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν κτίσις ἀφανὴς ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ, πάντα δὲ γυμνὰ καὶ τετραχηλισμένα τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς αὐτοῦ, πρὸς ὃν ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος.
records.gloss: And not is creature hidden before him, all [things] but naked and laid bare to the eyes of him, to whom for us the word.
pieces: No created thing is concealed from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. All things are stripped bare and open to the eyes of the one we must answer to.

L.13: And there is no creature hidden before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but all [things are] naked and laid open to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes, to whom [we must give our] account.

R.13: Nothing God has made can hide from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Everything stands bare and open before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one we must answer to.

decisions.choice: him: God
decisions.reason: The word of God in 4:12 passes into God himself, who speaks it: nothing can hide from him.

decisions.choice: laid open: exposed, helpless
decisions.reason: τραχηλίζομαι comes from the word for neck: to bend back the neck, as a wrestler does to an opponent or as a victim's throat is bared. Everything is exposed to God.

decisions.choice: the one to whom we must give account
alternatives: the one with whom we have to do
the one we are speaking about
decisions.reason: The phrase reads "to whom for us the word". λόγος here means an account, as of a debt or a life. The author plays on the word: the word God speaks to us (4:12), and the account we give to him.

decisions.choice: the one we must answer to
alternatives: to whom we must give account
decisions.reason: Plain words for giving an account.

decisions.choice: [we must give our] account
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the words the short Greek phrase leaves out.

records.source: Ἔχοντες οὖν ἀρχιερέα μέγαν διεληλυθότα τοὺς οὐρανούς, Ἰησοῦν τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ, κρατῶμεν τῆς ὁμολογίας·
records.gloss: Having therefore high priest great having passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of the God, let us hold fast the confession;
pieces: We have, then, a great high priest who has gone through the heavens: Jesus the Son of God. So let us keep a firm grip on the confession we make.

L.14: Having therefore a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast the confession;

R.14: Jesus, the Son of God, is our great high priest. He has gone through the heavens into God's presence. So let us hold on tightly to the faith we confess.

decisions.choice: passed through the heavens: as the high priest passed into the inner sanctuary
decisions.reason: On the Day of Atonement the high priest passed through the tent into the inner room before God (Leviticus 16). Jesus has passed through the heavens into God's presence (9:24).

decisions.choice: a great high priest: above every other high priest
decisions.reason: "Great" sets Jesus above the high priests of Israel (7:26-28; 10:21).

decisions.choice: hold fast the confession: keep holding on to the faith we declare
decisions.reason: ὁμολογία is the open declaration of faith in Jesus (3:1; 10:23).

decisions.choice: Son, capitalized
decisions.reason: The title of Christ, as in 1:2 and 3:6.

decisions.choice: the faith we confess
decisions.reason: Readable's book-wide rendering of this word.

decisions.choice: into God's presence
decisions.reason: Readable says where Jesus has gone, as 9:24 does.

records.heading: Jesus, the great high priest

records.source: οὐ γὰρ ἔχομεν ἀρχιερέα μὴ δυνάμενον συμπαθῆσαι ταῖς ἀσθενείαις ἡμῶν, πεπειρασμένον δὲ κατὰ πάντα καθ’ ὁμοιότητα χωρὶς ἁμαρτίας.
records.gloss: Not for we have high priest not being able to sympathize with the weaknesses of us, having been tested but in all [respects] according to likeness, without sin.
pieces: For the high priest we have is not one who cannot share the feeling of our weaknesses; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has been put to the test in every way, as we are, but without sinning.

L.15: For we have not a high priest unable to feel along with our weaknesses, but [one] who has been tested in all [ways] according to likeness, apart from sin.

R.15: Our high priest understands our weaknesses and feels them with us. He was tested in every way that we are, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} never sinned.

decisions.choice: feel along with: share the feeling, suffer with
decisions.reason: συμπαθέω is more than pity; it is feeling with someone (the same verb in 10:34).

decisions.choice: tested: put to the test, including temptation to sin
decisions.reason: πειράζω covers trials and temptations alike; Jesus suffered when he was tested (2:18). "Tempted" is the familiar rendering; the word includes it.

decisions.choice: in every way, as we are
alternatives: in every way, because he was like us
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean "in the same way as we are" or "in keeping with his likeness to us"; both point to 2:17, that he was made like his brothers and sisters in every way.

decisions.choice: apart from sin: he was tested without sinning
alternatives: tested in everything except what comes from a sinful nature
decisions.reason: The main sense is that he never gave in (7:26). The phrase can also mean that his testing did not come from sin within him; either way he was without sin.

decisions.choice: the high priest we have is not one who cannot ...
alternatives: we do not have a high priest who cannot ...
decisions.reason: A positive frame for the double negative.

records.source: προσερχώμεθα οὖν μετὰ παρρησίας τῷ θρόνῳ τῆς χάριτος, ἵνα λάβωμεν ἔλεος καὶ χάριν εὕρωμεν εἰς εὔκαιρον βοήθειαν.
records.gloss: Let us approach therefore with boldness the throne of the grace, so that we may receive mercy and grace we may find for well-timed help.
pieces: So let us, with confidence, approach the throne of grace, to receive mercy and to find grace that brings help just when we need it.

L.16: Let us therefore approach with boldness the throne of grace, so that we may receive mercy and may find grace for well-timed help.

R.16: So let us come near to God's throne, the place where grace is given. Let us come with confidence. There we will receive mercy, and we will find grace that helps us at the very moment we need it.

decisions.choice: approach: come near to God, as worshipers and priests do
decisions.reason: προσέρχομαι is used in the Greek Old Testament of priests and worshipers coming near to God; the letter uses it for believers (7:25; 10:22).

decisions.choice: the throne of grace: God's throne, from which grace is given
decisions.reason: The throne is God's; Jesus is seated at its right hand (8:1; 12:2). It is a throne marked by grace, where those who come receive help.

decisions.choice: with boldness: freely and openly, without fear
decisions.reason: παρρησία is the freedom of those who belong and may come in (3:6; 10:19).

decisions.choice: well-timed help: help that comes at the right moment
decisions.reason: εὔκαιρος means timely, coming when it is needed.

decisions.choice: confidence
decisions.reason: As in 3:6.

decisions.choice: come near
decisions.reason: Readable's book-wide rendering.

decisions.choice: God's throne, the place where grace is given
decisions.reason: Readable explains the phrase, as the meaning decision does.
